permissions.description: Call WebAir's semantic API (a fictional demo airline): search flights, read fare rules, request a booking quote and, only with the separate purchase permission, simulate a purchase.

Read the travel profile you choose from your memory (home airport, preferred cabin, nonstop preference) when a request leaves those unstated. The profile becomes search criteria sent to WebAir; it is never shown to a model as a profile.

Read the passenger identity you choose (name and contact email) and send it to WebAir for a booking quote or a simulated purchase, and nowhere else. No model sees it; the card before a purchase shows the name only.

Read which payment method you choose (an opaque demo identifier and a display label, never a card number) and send the identifier to WebAir with a simulated purchase, and nowhere else. No model sees it; the card before a purchase shows the label only.

Simulate purchasing the one quote this conversation made, with the payment method you choose, after the agent asks you with the quote's facts. Fictional: WebAir performs no real transaction and charges nothing. Consequential by design: grant it once, for one purchase.
Use the host-selected model router to interpret the request, choose fares and write the answer.
Read and write explicit worker state views for this turn only; the history, the known fares, the open quote and the confirmation outlive the turn as summaries.
After a booking quote or a simulated purchase, propose one travel preference to remember (a cabin, an airline, an airport). Nothing is written until you accept it after the run.

Run WebAir's fare-totals module (WebAssembly, no imports) to recompute each fare's total from its per-passenger price, so the totals WebAir states are checked on your device. It can only compute over the prices the graph gives it.
